Worshippers prostrated on their clothes' ends in heat; the Prophet prayed in shoes and after wiping khuffs, held his arms out wide, and Hudhaifa rejected an imperfectly performed prayer.
One praying speaks privately to his Lord, so he spits left or under his foot, not ahead or right, and prostrates without laying his forearms flat like a dog.
Malik bin Huwairith led a prayer only to show how the Prophet prayed, sitting briefly after the prostration before rising from the first rak'a.
The Prophet raised both hands shoulder-high at the opening, bowing and rising; people were ordered to place the right hand on the left forearm; he supplicated silently before reciting.
Followers watched the imam: Khabbab knew the Prophet recited in Zuhr and Asr from his moving beard, and Al-Bara's companions stood until they saw him prostrate.
Accused at Kufa of praying badly, Sa'd said he lengthened the first two rak'at as the Prophet did; a prayer without Al-Fatiha is invalid; a man is taught calm prayer.
The Prophet recited Al-Mursalat or At-Tur in Maghrib, At-Tin in Isha, sixty to a hundred verses in Fajr; Abu Huraira prostrated at Surah 84; Al-Fatiha alone suffices.
The Prophet recited aloud or quietly as ordered, Al-Fatiha and a surah in the first two rak'at, the first longer; love of Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad earns Paradise.
Say Amin when the imam says it, or says 'nor of those who go astray'; one whose Amin coincides with the angels' has his past sins forgiven.
Abu Bakra is told not to bow before reaching the row again; Ali, Abu Huraira and others said Takbir at every bowing, rising and prostration, as the Prophet did.
Hands rest on the knees in bowing; one who skimps bowing and prostration has not prayed; after the imam's 'Sami'a l-lahu liman hamidah' followers say 'Rabbana laka l-hamd'.
After rising from bowing came the Qunut, asking forgiveness for believers and invoking against disbelievers and Mudar; angels raced to record a man's praise; the Prophet stood straight and long.
The Prophet kept his arms off his sides in prayer; he was ordered to prostrate on seven bones: forehead with nose, hands, knees, toes, not tucking up clothes or hair.
Men with small Izars tied them round their necks, and women were told not to rise from prostration before the men sat up; prostration is on seven bones.
Glorifying Allah in bowing and prostration, sitting between prostrations, a brief sitting before rising, forearms off the ground, Takbir aloud, and sitting on the left foot.
The Tashahhud the Prophet taught instead of 'peace be on Allah', who is As-Salam, and supplications in prayer: refuge from the grave, the Dajjal, sin and debt, and forgiveness.
Mud marked the Prophet's forehead from prostrating; followers said the Taslim together with him, as at Itban's house, and he stayed seated while the women left.
After the Taslim the Prophet faced the people, once relaying Allah's words on crediting rain to stars; he waited for women to leave and once hurried to give away gold.
Prayer standing is best, sitting earns half its reward, lying half again; the unable sit or lie on their side, and the aged Prophet recited sitting, then stood to bow.
In his bowings and prostrations the Prophet used to glorify and praise Allah, our Lord, and ask Him for forgiveness.
On a journey the Prophet recited Surat at-Tin in one of the first two rak'at of the Isha prayer.
A man who prayed improperly greeted the Prophet, who returned his greeting and sent him back to pray, then taught him to recite, bow, prostrate and sit with calmness.
The Prophet told people to bow and prostrate properly, swearing that he sees them from behind his back.
Sent back three times to repeat his prayer, a man was taught to perform ablution, face the Qibla, say Takbir, recite, and bow, prostrate and sit until at rest.
